steps.say: The craniovertebral junction is where skull meets spine, and crowding here compresses the medulla with the upper cord. In basilar invagination the odontoid is pushed up into the foramen magnum, while in Chiari one the tonsils are pulled down. Both conditions are united by blocked fluid flow with a syrinx carved in the cord. Neck pain with downbeat nystagmus with weak hands is the classic warning.
steps.tx: The **craniovertebral junction** joins skull to spine, and crowding here squeezes medulla plus upper cord. **Basilar invagination** pushes the odontoid into the foramen magnum, while **Chiari I** pulls tonsils down over five mm. Both block **CSF flow** and carve a cord **syrinx**. Neck pain with downbeat nystagmus and hand weakness warns early.

steps.say: In Chiari one, the cerebellar tonsils are displaced more than five millimetres below the foramen magnum. Cough headache that bursts with strain is the signature, with downbeat nystagmus with hand tingling. A syrinx follows in about half the cases and hollows the cord from inside. Posterior fossa decompression with duraplasty is offered when symptoms progress or the syrinx grows.
steps.tx: **Chiari I** is tonsillar descent beyond **five mm** below the foramen magnum. **Cough headache** bursting on strain is the signature, with downbeat nystagmus and hand tingling. A **syrinx** follows in about half the cases. **Foramen magnum decompression** with duraplasty is offered for progressive symptoms or a growing syrinx.

steps.say: A syrinx is a fluid cavity inside the cord that spreads over years and burns out the hands first. Pain with temperature sense is lost in a cape pattern while touch is spared, which is called dissociated loss. Scoliosis with painless burns with wasted hands in a young adult is syringomyelia until proven otherwise. Draining the syrinx helps briefly, but fixing the Chiari above cures most.
steps.tx: A **syrinx** hollows the cord and burns out hands first over years. **Dissociated loss** (pain lost, touch spared) in a **cape pattern** is the signature. **Scoliosis** with painless burns and wasted hands in a young adult means syringomyelia. Fixing the **Chiari above** cures most; draining the syrinx alone recurs.

steps.say: Basilar invagination is diagnosed on M R I when the odontoid tip crosses Chamberlain line. Rheumatoid arthritis with Down syndrome with old trauma are the top causes. Progressive quadriparesis with torticollis with lower cranial nerve palsy follows. Traction with posterior fixation holds reducible cases, while the odontoid is removed through the mouth or nose when it cannot be pulled down.
steps.tx: **Basilar invagination** is odontoid crossing **Chamberlain line** on MRI. **Rheumatoid**, Down syndrome and old trauma cause most cases. Progressive quadriparesis with torticollis and lower cranial palsy follows. **Traction plus posterior fixation** holds reducible cases and fuses the spine; **transoral odontoidectomy** frees irreducible compression before fixation.

points: Pulls down with traction, fix from behind
left.title: Reducible

steps.say: Hydrocephalus means too much fluid inside the ventricles, either because flow is blocked or absorption has failed. Obstructive hydrocephalus enlarges only the chambers above the block, while communicating hydrocephalus swells them all. Aqueduct stenosis gives a classic triad of big lateral with third ventricles with a small fourth. E T V with shunting restores flow or drains it.
steps.tx: **Hydrocephalus** is excess ventricular CSF from **obstruction** or failed absorption. **Obstructive** hydrocephalus enlarges chambers above the block only. **Aqueduct stenosis** balloons lateral plus third ventricles with a small fourth. **Endoscopic third ventriculostomy** restores flow, and **shunting** drains when flow cannot be restored.

rows: Big lateral and third, small fourth

steps.say: A ventriculoperitoneal shunt drains fluid to the belly and is the commonest operation, but it blocks, infects and overdains. Headache with vomiting with a sleepy child with a shunt means blockage until proven otherwise, and fever with redness along the tube means infection. C T head is the first test, and a blocked shunt is revised urgently because pressure rises fast in children.
steps.tx: **Ventriculoperitoneal shunt** drains CSF to the belly but **blocks, infects and overdains**. Headache with vomiting and drowsiness in a shunted child means **blockage** first. Fever with redness along the tube means **infection**. **CT head** compares ventricle size with baseline, and a blocked shunt is **revised urgently**.

steps.say: Acute hydrocephalus after bleeding or meningitis kills quickly and is drained at the bedside. Sudden headache with vomiting with a falling conscious level with blown pupils is coning from pressure. An external ventricular drain is placed through a burr hole and set to drip at a safe height. Never perform a lumbar puncture when obstructive hydrocephalus is suspected, because it invites herniation.
steps.tx: **Acute hydrocephalus** after bleed or meningitis is drained at the bedside with an **external ventricular drain**. Falling consciousness with blown pupils means **coning**. The drain is set to drip at a safe height and weaned as the cause resolves. **Lumbar puncture is banned** in obstructive hydrocephalus because it invites herniation.

steps.say: Myelomeningocele drags the hindbrain down and causes Chiari two with hydrocephalus in almost every case. Periconceptional supplementation prevents most neural tube defects, which is why every planned pregnancy is covered. The back is closed within two days of birth, and the hydrocephalus is shunted when the head grows too fast. Leg function with bladder continence decides the long term outcome.
steps.tx: **Chiari II** complicates almost every **myelomeningocele** and causes hydrocephalus. **Supplementation** before conception prevents most defects. The sac is **closed within two days** of birth. **Shunting** follows when head growth crosses centiles. Leg power with **bladder continence** decides outcome, and latex allergy is screened.

steps.say: Every big head with every neck pain with every wasted hand follows the same imaging order. M R I brain with whole spine with C S F flow study comes first and shows the block with the syrinx. The descent is measured in millimetres, and the odontoid is judged against Chamberlain line. Flow restored by ventriculostomy or a shunt is confirmed on follow up scans, and syrinx shrinkage proves success.
steps.tx: **Workup order** is fixed: **MRI brain plus spine** with CSF flow study first. **Descent in mm** grades Chiari, and the odontoid is judged on **Chamberlain line**. **Flow study** picks ventriculostomy versus shunt candidates. Follow up MRI must show a **shrinking syrinx**; growth means the decompression has failed.

nodes.label: MRI brain and spine with flow
Syrinx must shrink on follow up

steps.say: An untreated syrinx hollows the cord to a useless tube and leaves deformed arms with a bent spine. Shunt infection seeds the belly with meningitis and needs full removal with antibiotics. Overdrainage collapses the ventricles into slit syndrome with crippling posture headaches. But a timely decompression with a working shunt gives most children a normal school life, which is why follow up never ends.
steps.tx: **Complications** shape counselling: untreated syrinx leaves wasted arms with scoliosis. **Shunt infection** needs removal with antibiotics. **Overdrainage** gives slit ventricles with postural headache. **Tethered cord** with latex allergy complicates myelomeningocele. Timely **decompression** with a working shunt returns most children to normal schooling.

steps.say: For the exam, lock in five millimetres for Chiari one, cape dissociated loss for syrinx, Chamberlain line for invagination, small fourth ventricle for aqueduct block, and never tap an obstructive hydrocephalus. Management is always surgery or drainage, never tablets. Memorise the facts in this table exactly as written and match each scan sign with its block.
steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** tonsils beyond **five mm** mark Chiari I. **Cape dissociated loss** marks syrinx. **Chamberlain line** judges invagination. Small fourth with big lateral ventricles marks **aqueduct** block. **Lumbar puncture is banned** in obstructive hydrocephalus, and a blocked shunt is revised urgently.
